description: Declarative registry of binary-anchored offset detectors for RS3ProjectXUpdater. Each anchor maps one or more engine offsets (Offsets.kt) to a RELIABLE in-binary code location whose disassembly directly encodes the offset, plus a structural extraction recipe (the `extract` DSL). EXPORT fills sig_blob/sig_mask/feat_hash and resolves old_value against the OLD binary; IMPORT re-resolves against the NEW binary and flags drift (new_value != old_value). `old_value` is hand-seeded from the verified Offsets.kt and acts as a sanity bound. `validated:true` means the recipe was confirmed by hand against a live binary this session; `false` means seed/best-effort, to be confirmed by the export self-test (IMPORT against the source build must reproduce old_value).

steps: find       {match, dst?, src?, mem?:{base,index,scale,disp}, imm?, occurrence?} — scan forward from entry for the Nth matching instruction; sets the cursor
find_after {same as find} — scan forward from the current cursor (after the previous step)
capture    {from:'mem.disp'|'imm', as:VAR} — record a displacement or immediate into VAR (attached to the matched instruction of the preceding find)
rip_target {match, as:VAR} — capture the absolute resolved target of a RIP-relative MOV/LEA
back_scan  {from_call:FUNC, match, mem:{base,...}, capture, occurrence?} — from a CALL to FUNC, scan backwards for a [base+disp] load
call_arg   {call:FUNC, arg:N, capture} — capture disp of `LEA argRegN,[base+disp]` immediately before a CALL to FUNC

dst_reg accepts the ABI-neutral token '@this', resolved to RDI on SysV/ELF and RCX on Win64/PE. NEVER hardcode a register name in a recipe: it silently matches an unrelated instruction on the other platform (a literal "RDI" made OPathingEntity.HITMARKS_AND_HEADBARS resolve to garbage on the PE).
dsl.operands: register placeholders: '@name' binds a register on first use and refers to it after; '*' is wildcard. mem match fields are optional; scale/disp matched only when present.
dsl.emit: value is an integer expression over captured vars and hex/dec consts using + - * << (). One anchor may emit multiple offsets via emit[]. min(a,b) and max(a,b) are also available. Use them when the two platforms emit the same pair of accesses in a different ORDER, so an occurrence-indexed capture cannot be relied on to mean the same field on both.
dsl.manager_class: ALTERNATIVE to anchor/extract: an anchor with {"manager_class":"jag::SomeManager","min_sites":N,"disp_min":"0x400","disp_max":"0x20000"} resolves by CONSENSUS — the tool scans every CALL to a method of that C++ class and reads the preceding `MOV/LEA RDI,[client+OFF]` this-load; the most common OFF (in [disp_min,disp_max], default 0x400-0x20000) wins. This is the most reliable OClient-pointer anchor (many independent callsites agree) and needs no anchor function. CRITICAL: keep disp_min high enough to exclude nested-object this-loads (this=[parent+0x20]) which can otherwise out-count the real client offset. min_sites guards weak consensus. Discover the class->offset map for a new build with `dump managers[:lo-hi]`; find where field-read managers are stored with `dump ctorstores:*@lo-hi`.
dsl.portability: A recipe must resolve on BOTH the ELF and the PE build of the same client. The three things that break portability: (1) hardcoded registers - use '@this'; (2) absolute disp_min/disp_max windows tuned to one build's struct layout - the same struct can sit at a different offset on the other ABI, and a window that is correct for one can select the WRONG field on the other; (3) occurrence-indexed captures where the compilers order the accesses differently - disambiguate with min()/max() or a semantic delta instead.

ofunctions_note: OFunctions consts -> qualified function name. IMPORT resolves each via the function sig-match (functions.ndjson) and emits the full OFunctions block into offsets_<ver>.kt. These are absolute function addresses (they move every build), so no drift flag.

jag::graphics::WorldToScreen (949-1 @0xa6e2b0) projects a world-space AABB to screen; its matrix args are (out, arg2=viewMatrix, arg3=scaleMatrix, arg4=projectionMatrix). Callers (e.g. the entity-projection helper @0x3ca1a0) issue `LEA RSI,[World+VIEW]; LEA RDX,[World+SCALE]; LEA RCX,[World+PROJECTION]` directly before the CALL, so call_arg arg2 => VIEW_MATRIX and call_arg arg4 => PROJECTION_MATRIX. CRITICAL: PROJECTION is arg4 (the combined view*proj @0x13200 that WorldToScreen actually samples for screen x/y), NOT arg3 (the middle SCALE matrix @0x13180 that the old Mat4x4Multiply-caller recipe wrongly emitted as projection). via_caller picks the first caller whose args are BOTH direct LEAs; callers that pass projection via a register alias (MOV RCX,R14) fail call_arg and are skipped automatically.

Emitted by the WorldToScreen anchor as call_arg arg4 (the combined view*proj matrix WorldToScreen samples). 949-1 = 0x13200 (VIEW 0x13100 + 0x100). Re-seeded from the stale 948-5 0x131e0; 0x13180 is the middle SCALE matrix, NOT projection.

Callers reach the embedded HeightMap subobject as `<this> = World + HEIGHT_MAP` before CALL GetFineHeight. This uses back_scan rather than call_arg because the two compilers emit that address computation differently: the ELF build emits `LEA arg1,[World+disp]` but the PE build emits `ADD RCX,disp` on a register that already holds the World. call_arg only matches LEA, so it silently found nothing on the PE; back_scan's this-load reader handles LEA, MOV and ADD/SUB-immediate alike. dst_reg is '@this' so the register is resolved per ABI.

jag::game::World::GetMapSquare is the world->mapsquare index accessor. Both builds subtract the two origin fields from the arguments and then load the mapsquares vector (outer stride 0x18), but they do it in OPPOSITE order: the ELF build subtracts Y first, the PE build subtracts X first. The old occurrence-indexed recipe therefore assigned X and Y the wrong way round on the PE. X_OFFSET is always the lower of the two displacements on both builds, so the pair is disambiguated with min()/max() instead of by order. X_MAX and Y_MAX are derived: the four build-area bounds are contiguous dwords in the order X_OFFSET, Y_OFFSET, X_MAX, Y_MAX on both builds (verified independently against the World constructor's argument stores and against the double-loop scene walker on each). MAPSQUARES_VECTOR is captured independently as the first 64-bit load after the two subtractions. The disp window is deliberately wide enough to span both layouts, which is safe because the recipe runs inside GetMapSquare, whose only struct accesses are these.
Emitted by the World::GetMapSquare anchor (see OWorld.MAPSQUARE_X_OFFSET).
Emitted by the World::GetMapSquare anchor (see OWorld.MAPSQUARE_X_OFFSET). Outer 2D vector triple, stride 0x18 outer / 0x8 inner.

The World ctor jag::game::World::World (949-1 @0x4c4620) constructs a graphics::GraphNode and stores it at World+ROOT_GRAPH_NODE (`MOV [World+0x10170], graphNodePtr`, param_1[0x202e]). The window 0x10169-0x1017f isolates the root ptr from the AABB float area just below it (0x10130-0x10168; the old 948-5 root offset 0x10150 now lives inside that AABB) and the SSE zero-init at 0x10180 above it. occ1 MOV-mem in that window = 0x10170. Window is tight by necessity (root is 0x8 above the AABB); a larger future drift reports UNRESOLVED, which is still a drift signal.

GetLocationContainerAt reads `CMP qword [ms+0x70],0` to select chunkSize 16 vs 8. First such compare in the function. LINUX-CONFIRMED (949-4): GetLocationContainerAt@0x4991a0 computes chunkSize = (*(long*)(this+0x70)==0) ? 16 : 8 via the `(-(uint)(x==0) & 8) + 8` idiom, so CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG and COMPOSITE_DATA are the SAME field at +0x70.

Same accessor as OMapSquare.CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG. GetLocationContainerAt (949-1 @0x4991a0) reads the location-container 2D vector base as its FIRST instruction `MOV R8,[MapSquare+0xeb80]` (then +0xeb88 = vector end). occ1 MOV-mem in window 0xe800-0xf000 = 0xeb80. +0x18 vs 948-5 (0xeb68). Outer stride 0x18 / inner 0x8 (raw LC ptrs).

VALIDATED (windowed): animationId is a plain int32 at entity+0xa88 (-1 = none), accessed polymorphically across the binary (NOT set in the small base Entity::Entity @0x13f310). jag::NPCList::ProcessNpcInfo has a single `CMP reg,dword[npc+0xa88]` (the per-tick animation check). The disp window 0xa00-0xb00 isolates it from other field reads. This anchor CONFIRMS the value and DETECTS drift within the window; if animationId moves outside 0xa00-0xb00 the recipe reports UNRESOLVED (still a drift signal). The -1 writer is FUN_00464850 `MOV dword[entity+0xa88],0xffffffff`.

HitmarksAndHeadbars is a POINTER field on PathingEntity; the caller does `MOV <this>,[entity+HMH]` immediately before CALL AddHeadbar. dst_reg is '@this' rather than a literal register - the previous literal "RDI" matched an unrelated RDI write on the PE and produced the nonsense value 0xffffffffffffff98, which shipped in the Windows offset table. The disp window rejects stack spills so the scan walks past them. (The call is deep inside the large ProcessExtendedInfo functions - needs RECIPE_MAX_INSNS >= ~4000.)

MANAGER_CLASS anchor — consensus over every callsite of a jag::NPCList method: each loads `MOV/LEA RDI,[client+0x194b8]` (the this-arg) before the CALL. 17/17 sites agree. This is the most reliable manager-offset anchor available.

MANAGER_CLASS anchor — callsites of jag::ConnectionManager methods load `RDI,[client+0x19440]`. min_sites lowered 10->2 for 949-1: only ~6-7 CM methods are named in this build (vs many in 948-5), and most intra-CM calls pass `this` in a register, so the agreeing this-load count is small (~2-3 clean sites at 0x19440). One outlier at 0x194a8 comes from LoginProtocolHandler (operates on MainLogicManager, client+0x194a8); 0x19440 still wins by count. Naming more CM methods in future builds will raise the margin.
MANAGER_CLASS anchor — 37/37 callsites of jag::game::SceneManager methods load `RDI,[client+0x19558]`.

MANAGER_CLASS anchor — 18/26 callsites of jag::InterfaceManager methods load `RDI,[client+0x19488]`. (Field is named INTERFACE_LIST in Offsets.kt; the C++ class is InterfaceManager.) min_sites lowered 5->3: the PE build has far fewer InterfaceManager methods named, and requiring 5 distinct callsites made the consensus abstain on a class whose offset every callsite agrees on.

Depends on WorldList::InsertOrReplace being named in the build; if the manager class has no named methods the consensus fails (as it did before this re-baseline). Low site count (2) — MEDIUM confidence.

VALIDATED (windowed): StatTable (0x73a0) and ClientVarDomain (0x73a8) are ADJACENT member pointers in MainLogicManager. StatTable::UpdateStat and ClientVarDomain::SetVarValue have NO direct xrefs (vtable/inlined) so caller back_scan fails. Every caller of jag::ProjectileList::Add loads the list as `MOV <this>,[client+PROJECTILE_LIST]` before the call. jag::ProjectileList::Add is in the OFunctions set so it is guaranteed to be named on both builds, which makes this a portable substitute for a manager_class consensus (there is only one named ProjectileList method, so consensus would abstain). The disp window keeps the scan from latching onto a nested-object this-load or a stack spill.

Anchored on ReadTileFlags rather than on the HasBridgeFlag wrapper: HasBridgeFlag exists as a real function on both builds, but MSVC ALSO inlines it at ~20 sites, so anchoring there samples an unrepresentative subset of callers. ReadTileFlags is the common leaf both wrappers funnel into. back_scan (not call_arg) for the same reason as OWorld.HEIGHT_MAP: the PE computes the subobject address with `ADD RCX,disp`, which call_arg's LEA-only scan misses. Cross-check: LINK_MAP sits exactly 0x10 above HEIGHT_MAP on both builds.

verified_fields._doc: Struct fields established by hand against a specific build, for values no anchor recipe can derive. Emitted BEFORE anchors and OFunctions so anything the tooling can re-derive from the binary wins. Each row records the build it was verified against; on a later build the value is still emitted (dropping it would silently disable engine features) but is downgraded to STALE_CARRY and flagged needs_reverification, so it surfaces as work to redo rather than as a trusted number. ONLY put a field here if a specific instruction in the target binary proves it - predictions and unresolved fields are deliberately left OUT so the engine throws OffsetUnavailableException instead of reading garbage.

Named .data label jag::g_client. The app entry point stores jag::Client::Client()'s return value straight into it (`plVar5 = jag::Client::Client(client); jag::g_app = plVar5; jag::g_client = plVar5;`) after allocating 0x53818 bytes - large enough for the client fields the manager anchors resolve around 0x19800-0x19f80 - and the shutdown path clears it to 0 right after destroying jag::g_app. The OGlobal.CLIENT ANCHOR CANNOT FIRE ON THE PE: it keys on jag::packethandlers::ClientState::MINIMAP_FLAG_SET, which carries no symbol in either PE build. A future portable recipe could instead take the caller of the (named) jag::Client::Client and rip_target its store, which would make this self-maintaining. Recorded here because the offset tables are rebuilt from the previous build's table, which DROPS every absolute address as un-carryable; this value was previously present only as a hand-written entry in the generated engine JSON and was therefore destroyed by the next regeneration.

withheld_fields._doc: Field ids whose shipped value has been DISPROVED against the target binary but whose correct offset has not been located. They are deliberately NOT carried into the generated tables: the engine accessor then throws OffsetUnavailableException, which fails loudly, instead of dereferencing an offset that analysis has shown points at a different field or past the end of the object. The declaration stays in Offsets.kt - this list is a to-do, not a deletion. Remove an entry the moment the correct offset is established (and record it in verified_fields or as an anchor recipe). Applies to both platforms unless placed under a platform key.

common.evidence: Shipped 0xe is the PARENT LAYER COMPONENT ID, not a type. jag::opcode::_if_getlayer returns (interfaceId<<16)|comp[+0xe] with 0xffff meaning no parent layer, and jag::InterfaceManager::GetParentLayer indexes the interface's static component array with it. The real type is not a struct field in this build: jag::opcode::_cc_create maps the 0..0x1c cache type through the 29-byte table at 0x01076260 only to pick a ui-category for the parent's accept-child virtual, and passes the raw type to the component factory, which switches on it to allocate one of twelve differently-sized C++ subclasses. Nothing stores the type back on the object - the class identity IS the type, readable only by calling the vtable slot that returns the per-subclass class-id constant (a search for a store of one of those constants finds none; only a constant-returning stub). A correct value would require the engine to resolve the type from the vptr rather than read a field, so no offset is emitted.

Shipped 0x60 is a scalar pointer constructor argument (jag::game::LocationContainer::LocationContainer stores an argument there and a byte constant at +0x68, so the pair cannot be a vector begin/end). The two values were taken from a different class - the loc-change manager reached from the Client, whose pending vector really is begin/end/capacity at those offsets (jag::game::ApplyLocChange). LocationContainer has exactly three category vectors plus the dispatch-slot table, all of which the engine already declares; there is no fourth 'dynamic' vector, and server-spawned locations land in the same three vectors and slots.
Second half of the same borrowed pair; see OLocationContainer.DYNAMIC_LOCATIONS_BEGIN.

Shipped 0x8 is the Entity base's GraphNode pointer, written by the constructor from a GraphNode factory and later passed to jag::graphics::GraphNode::UpdateBounds. LocationContainer contains no red-black tree; its locations live in the three category vectors and the dispatch-slot table.

Shipped 0x10 is the Entity kind discriminator byte (constructor writes 9; sibling classes write 4 and 0xA and it is read back through a switch), not a tree root. Same reasoning as the sentinel entry. Note both shipped values also collide exactly with this object's ENTRY_LOCATION_PTR_OFFSET and ENTRY_STRIDE constants, which is where the numbers came from.

Copied from jag::game::Location, whose layout is unrelated. sizeof(CombinedLocationSection) is 0x110, so the shipped value reads past the end of the object into the pool. The complete-object destructor enumerates every refcounted member and there is no render-node shared_ptr among them. The section reaches its renderable indirectly through its GraphNode, as the class's own mesh pick test shows; recovering this properly means modelling that hop, not naming an offset.
Control-block half of the same copied pair; see OCombinedLocationSection.RENDER_NODE.
Also past the end of the 0x110-byte object. The complete-object destructor lists every pointer member the class owns and no parent-CombinedLocation pointer is among them.

parked_anchors.notes:
PARKED - deliberately NOT in the executing anchors list; the four OMapSquare values are supplied by verified_fields instead. Kept verbatim so a future session can revive it once the recipe matcher can discriminate operand width on a STORE.
Layout is settled and identical on both 949-4 builds: the constructor writes mapsquareX and mapsquareY as two adjacent dwords, then the ClientCompositeData shared_ptr as {control block, object} in the next two qwords, with the strong count incremented through the control block - which is what makes COUNTER the lower qword and DATA the upper. The four emitted offsets are therefore x, x+4, x+0xc, x+0x14.
WHY IT CANNOT RUN TODAY: the capture wants the first dword store to the object in a small window, but the window is bracketed by a byte store and a qword store to neighbouring offsets, and operandSizeMatches resolves width from the WRITTEN REGISTER - which is null for a store, so it abstains and the recipe captures whichever neighbour comes first. Measured on the ELF: with the window opened wide it captured the constructor's own argument spill (a stack slot, base RSP) and emitted a plausible-looking but wrong quad; narrowed past the spill it captured the byte store instead. Two attempted matcher fixes - rejecting stack-based operands, and reading the x86 size prefix off the memory operand - were both reverted rather than shipped half-working, because operandSizeMatches is shared by every other recipe in this file and a regression there is far more expensive than one parked anchor. A correct revival needs operand width taken from the instruction's memory operand (verified against a store, not just a register write), after which this recipe with a stack-excluding base resolves to the right dword on both the ELF and the PE.
REPLACES A KNOWN-BAD SET: the shipping tables carried a different quad for these four on BOTH platforms; those values are not these fields (one is an unrelated qword sentinel whose value is never tested, one has no MapSquare-relative use at all, and two fall inside the embedded polymorphic subobject). The giveaway was that CHUNK_SIZE_FLAG and COMPOSITE_DATA are the same field yet the table gave them different offsets.

_parked_anchors_doc: Anchor recipes whose target layout is understood but which the recipe matcher cannot currently express safely. They are NOT executed. Their values live in verified_fields, so the table stays correct while the recipe waits for the matcher capability it needs. Move an entry back into 'anchors' only after proving it resolves to the right value on BOTH platform builds.
